en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pāpanivāriya Hatthivagga 10 I was a king named Mahāpajjota, ruling over the kingdom of Kāsī. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, arrived at Benares. Having heard that the Blessed One had arrived, I went out from the city to meet him. Having approached the Blessed One, I paid homage to him and sat down to one side. As I was sitting there, the Blessed One taught me the Dhamma with its many aspects and its various modes, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening me. Having been taught the Dhamma by the Blessed One with its many aspects and its various modes, having been encouraged, inspired, and gladdened, I rose from my seat, circumambulated the Blessed One keeping him to my right, and departed. Then, having returned to my own residence, I had a great pavilion constructed. Having had it prepared, I invited the Blessed One together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus for the meal on the following day. Having invited him, I returned to my own residence and prepared various kinds of fine food, both hard and soft. When the night had passed, I had the time announced: "It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready.

Then, knowing the time, the Blessed One, dressed in the morning and taking his bowl and robe, entered the city of Benares for alms. After walking for alms in Benares, he returned from his almsround, ate his meal, and set out for the great pavilion. At that time, I was standing outside the gate of the city, waiting for the Blessed One. Seeing the Blessed One approaching from afar, I went out to meet him. Having approached the Blessed One, I took his bowl and robe and escorted him into the city. Having led him to the great pavilion, I washed his feet and arranged a seat. Having prepared the seat, I informed the Blessed One: "The seat is ready, venerable sir; let the Blessed One sit down. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Once the Blessed One was seated, I washed his feet myself. Having washed his feet, I offered him water for drinking. Then, having served the Blessed One with my own hands various kinds of fine food, both hard and soft, until he was satisfied, when the Blessed One had finished eating and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, I took a low stool and sat down to one side. As I was sitting there, I requested of the Blessed One: "May the Blessed One accept my invitation for the three-month rains retreat. The Blessed One consented by remaining silent. Knowing his consent, I rose from my seat, circumambulated the Blessed One keeping him to my right, and departed. Then, having returned to my own residence, I had a great hall constructed. Having had it prepared, I provided it with all the requisites: beds, seats, mattresses, pillows, and lamps. Having provided it thus, I invited the Blessed One together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus for the three-month rains retreat. Having invited him, I returned to my own residence and prepared various kinds of fine food, both hard and soft. “The walking path of the Blessed One Piyadassi has been cleared by me;
it was covered with reeds.”
It wards off wind and heat.
For the purpose of avoiding evil and for the attainment of the wholesome;
For the abandoning of the defilements,
I strove in the Teacher’s dispensation.
In the eleventh aeon from now,
Known as Aggideva,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Pāpanivāriya spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Pāpanivāriya.
The twenty-second chapter, the Hatthivagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
The elephant, the sandal, and the truth,
the one-perceiver, and the rayed one.
Sandhita and Tālavaṇṭa,
as well as Akkantasaññaka;
Sappi and Pāpanivārī—
"Forty-five verses."
